def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import re

    def merge_status(prev: str | None, new: str) -> str:
        # fail dominates, then pass, then skip
        if prev is None:
            return new
        order = {"fail": 3, "pass": 2, "skip": 1}
        return new if order[new] > order[prev] else prev

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    # ---- Pre-normalise for common Rust/powershell wrapping artifacts ----
    # 1) join "o\nok" -> "ok", "fini\nished" -> "finished", etc. (only common tokens)
    # Do it conservatively for patterns seen in Rust harness output.
    log2 = log
    log2 = re.sub(r"(?<=\.)\n(?=\.\.)", "", log2)  # "...\n..." -> "......" (rare)
    log2 = re.sub(r"\.\.\.\s*o\s*\n\s*ok\b", "... ok", log2, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    log2 = re.sub(r"\bfini\s*\n\s*ished\b", "finished", log2, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    log2 = re.sub(r"\bdependencie\s*\n\s*es\b", "dependencies", log2, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    log2 = re.sub(r"\bdependen\s*\n\s*ncy\b", "dependency", log2, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    log2 = re.sub(r"\bpath\s*\n\s*hs\b", "paths", log2, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    # 2) ensure word boundary after ok/FAILED/ignored when immediately followed by text (e.g., "okLocked!")
    log2 = re.sub(r"\b(ok|ignored|FAILED)(?=[A-Za-z_])", r"\1 ", log2)

    # ---- 1) Rust libtest lines: "test name ... ok/FAILED/ignored" ----
    rust_line_re = re.compile(
        r"(?m)^\s*test\s+(?P<name>.+?)\s+\.\.\.\s+(?P<status>ok|ignored|FAILED|fail)\b",
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )
    for m in rust_line_re.finditer(log2):
        name = m.group("name").strip()
        status_raw = m.group("status").lower()
        status = "pass" if status_raw == "ok" else "skip" if status_raw == "ignored" else "fail"
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    # ---- 2) Go test: "--- PASS: TestName", "--- FAIL: TestName", "--- SKIP: TestName" ----
    go_re = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*---\s+(PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+([^\s]+)")
    for m in go_re.finditer(log2):
        status_raw, name = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        status = {"PASS": "pass", "FAIL": "fail", "SKIP": "skip"}[status_raw]
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    # ---- 3) pytest: "file.py::test_name PASSED/FAILED/SKIPPED/ERROR/XFAIL" ----
    pytest_re = re.compile(
        r"(?m)^\s*([^\s:][^:\n]*::[^\s]+)\s+(PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS)\b"
    )
    for m in pytest_re.finditer(log2):
        name, st = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
        status = "pass" if st in ("PASSED", "XPASS") else "skip" if st in ("SKIPPED", "XFAIL") else "fail"
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    # ---- 4) unittest-ish: "TestClass.test_method ... ok/FAIL/ERROR/skipped" ----
    unittest_re = re.compile(r"(?m)^\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)+)\s+\.\.\.\s+(ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped)\b")
    for m in unittest_re.finditer(log2):
        name, st = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2).lower()
        status = "pass" if st == "ok" else "skip" if st == "skipped" else "fail"
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    # ---- 5) Inline JUnit XML (if present in log) ----
    # Minimal XML parsing via regex (robust enough for inline logs).
    if "<testcase" in log2 and "<testsuite" in log2:
        # Capture testcase blocks (self-closing or with nested tags)
        tc_re = re.compile(r"<testcase\b([^>]*)>(.*?)</testcase\s*>|<testcase\b([^>]*)/>", re.DOTALL)
        attr_re = re.compile(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"')
        for m in tc_re.finditer(log2):
            attrs = m.group(1) or m.group(3) or ""
            body = m.group(2) or ""
            attr_map = {k: v for k, v in attr_re.findall(attrs)}
            name = attr_map.get("name")
            classname = attr_map.get("classname")
            if not name:
                continue
            full = f"{classname}::{name}" if classname else name
            if re.search(r"<skipped\b", body):
                status = "skip"
            elif re.search(r"<failure\b|<error\b", body):
                status = "fail"
            else:
                status = "pass"
            results[full] = merge_status(results.get(full), status)

    return results

def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import re
    from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    def set_result(name: str, status: str) -> None:
        name = (name or "").strip()
        if not name:
            return
        prev = results.get(name)
        # Prefer fail > skip > pass if duplicated
        if prev == "fail":
            return
        if prev == "skip" and status == "pass":
            return
        results[name] = status

    # ---------------- XML (JUnit-ish) ----------------
    xml_candidate = log.strip()
    if "<testsuite" in xml_candidate and "<testcase" in xml_candidate:
        def parse_xml(xml_text: str) -> bool:
            try:
                root = ET.fromstring(xml_text)
            except Exception:
                return False
            testcases = root.findall(".//testcase") if root.tag != "testcase" else [root]
            for tc in testcases:
                name = tc.get("name") or ""
                classname = tc.get("classname") or ""
                full = f"{classname}::{name}".strip(":")
                status = "pass"
                if tc.find("skipped") is not None:
                    status = "skip"
                elif tc.find("failure") is not None or tc.find("error") is not None:
                    status = "fail"
                set_result(full or name, status)
            return True

        if parse_xml(xml_candidate):
            return results
        for m in re.finditer(r"(<testsuite\b[\s\S]*?</testsuite>)", log):
            parse_xml(m.group(1))
        if results:
            return results

    # ---------------- Line-oriented parsing ----------------
    status_map = {
        "ok": "pass",
        "PASSED": "pass",
        "PASS": "pass",
        "FAILED": "fail",
        "FAIL": "fail",
        "ERROR": "fail",
        "ignored": "skip",
        "SKIPPED": "skip",
        "SKIP": "skip",
        "skipped": "skip",
        "XFAIL": "skip",
        "XPASS": "fail",
    }

    # libtest canonical line
    libtest_line_re = re.compile(
        r"^\s*test\s+(?P<name>.+?)\s+\.\.\.\s+(?P<status>ok|FAILED|ignored)\s*$"
    )

    # other frameworks (fallbacks)
    pytest_re = re.compile(
        r"^\s*(?P<name>\S+::\S+)\s+(?P<status>PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|XFAIL|XPASS|ERROR)\s*$"
    )
    gotest_re = re.compile(r"^\s*---\s+(?P<status>PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(?P<name>\S+)")
    unittest_re = re.compile(
        r"^\s*(?P<name>[\w./:-]+)\s+\.\.\.\s+(?P<status>ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped)\s*$"
    )

    # Wrapped libtest handling (PowerShell/terminal hard-wrap)
    buffering = False
    buf = ""

    # Abort buffering if we see clearly unrelated multi-line output
    abort_re = re.compile(
        r"^\s*(Running\s+(unittests|tests|doctests)\b|running\s+\d+\s+tests\b|test result:|failures:|error:|thread\s+'.+'\s+panicked)\b",
        re.IGNORECASE,
    )

    def extract_all_libtests_from_buffer(s: str) -> None:
        """
        The log capture sometimes concatenates multiple 'test ... ... ok' records
        into one long wrapped line. Extract *all* occurrences.
        """
        # Normalize whitespace a bit, but keep as a single string.
        norm = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)

        # Find all occurrences of: 'test <name> ... <status>'
        for m in re.finditer(r"\btest\s+(.+?)\s+\.\.\.\s+(ok|FAILED|ignored)\b", norm):
            name = m.group(1).strip()
            st = status_map.get(m.group(2), "fail")
            set_result(name, st)

    for raw_line in log.splitlines():
        line = raw_line.rstrip("\r\n")

        # If buffering a wrapped "test ..." record, append and try to extract.
        if buffering:
            if abort_re.match(line) and not line.lstrip().startswith("test "):
                buffering = False
                buf = ""
            else:
                # Preserve a space between lines; hard-wrap may happen mid-word but this is
                # preferable to accidentally concatenating "... ok" + "test ..." into a name.
                buf = (buf + " " + line.strip()).strip()

                # If we have at least one complete status token, try extracting all tests.
                if re.search(r"\.\.\.\s*(ok|FAILED|ignored)\b", buf):
                    extract_all_libtests_from_buffer(buf)
                    buffering = False
                    buf = ""
                elif len(buf) > 4096:
                    buffering = False
                    buf = ""
            continue

        # Single-line libtest
        m = libtest_line_re.match(line)
        if m:
            set_result(m.group("name"), status_map.get(m.group("status"), "fail"))
            continue

        # Begin buffering if it looks like a test line start
        if line.lstrip().startswith("test "):
            buffering = True
            buf = line.strip()
            # In case it already contains a status (but didn't match due to odd spacing),
            # try to extract immediately.
            if re.search(r"\.\.\.\s*(ok|FAILED|ignored)\b", buf):
                extract_all_libtests_from_buffer(buf)
                buffering = False
                buf = ""
            continue

        # Fallbacks
        m = pytest_re.match(line)
        if m:
            set_result(m.group("name"), status_map.get(m.group("status"), "fail"))
            continue

        m = gotest_re.match(line)
        if m:
            set_result(m.group("name"), status_map.get(m.group("status"), "fail"))
            continue

        m = unittest_re.match(line)
        if m:
            set_result(m.group("name"), status_map.get(m.group("status"), "fail"))
            continue

    # Flush if log ends mid-buffer
    if buffering and buf:
        extract_all_libtests_from_buffer(buf)

    return results

problem_statement:
"exact" modifier does not seem to work (at least when used in a revset within a describe() expression)
## Description

<!-- Thanks for your report! Please describe your problem or request here.
For questions, use https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj/discussions/new instead.
Feel free to remove any of the sections below if they don't seem useful. -->


## Steps to Reproduce the Problem

1. jj new -m "my_unique_test_description"
1. jj log -r "describe(exact:"my_unique_test_description")
1. Returns no revisions

## Expected Behavior

It should return the revisions exactly matching "my_unique_test_description" (normally it should just be one)

## Actual Behavior
No revisions are matched

## Specifications

- Platform: Windows
- Version: 0.24
hints_text:
Does `exact` mean that the entire content matches exactly or that an exact match is contained in the content?
I've run into this before. I think it's because technically, the description ends with a newline if it's non-empty. So `description(exact:"")` matches empty description, and `description(exact:"my_unique_test_description\n")` matches "my_unique_test_description".
> I've run into this before. I think it's because technically, the description ends with a newline if it's non-empty. So `description(exact:"")` matches empty description, and `description(exact:"my_unique_test_description\n")` matches "my_unique_test_description".

That's probably it. I think the revset doc can be updated.
Another confusing thing is that `description(exact:'my_unique_test_description\n')` doesn't work. A literal newline like

```shell
jj log -r 'description(exact:\'test
\')'
```

or

```shell
jj log -r "description(exact:'test
')"
```

does work (in `fish` at least).

Perhaps `description` should match both with and without a trailing `\n`, since `jj` already adds the `\n` automatically? I suppose we could have `strict_description` that acts differently. This isn't perfect, but perhaps it's better than the status quo. Or can we think of something even better?

I suppose there could be a version of `exact` that trims whitespace.
Well, `''` means raw string (i.e disable escapes).

I don't think exact match on description is useful (except for `exact:""`.) It's probably better to suggest regex for line-based matching than adding special case for `description()`.
What may be useful is having a query (and template?) for only the subject line of a description, which can be fairly useful to search exactly (e.g. commit subjects mentioned in emails), and could naturally strip the trailing newline.
> I don't think exact match on description is useful (except for exact:"".) It's probably better to suggest regex for line-based matching than adding special case for description()

I think it could be quite useful if you use certain specific descriptions for certain revisions (e.g. CI/CD, etc).
In any case, the current behavior is _very_ surprising. If you set the description to "test" by using `jj describe -m "test"` one would expect to find that specific revision by doing `jj log -r "description(exact:'test')", wouldn't it? The fact that jj adds a trailing '\n' should not leak to the UX, IMHO.

> What may be useful is having a query (and template?) for only the subject line of a description, which can be fairly useful to search exactly (e.g. commit subjects mentioned in emails), and could naturally strip the trailing newline.

FWIW mercurial does have a "matching" function that can take "summary" as its "field" argument, which looks for the first line of each commit message.
FWIW, `jj describe -m` has added since PR #936. `git commit -m` seems to do the same thing but `hg commit -m` does not.
Since due to PR #936 it is _not_ possible to have a description without a final new line, it seems to me that it would make sense for `exact` to automatically add a new line to the query string (if it is not already there). Otherwise it will _never_ return any result, which is very surprising given the example I provided above (i.e. doing `jj describe -m "test"` and then `jj log -r "description(exact:'test')"` and not getting any result).

I'm willing to try to create a PR for this if you think this would be a good solution.
> it seems to me that it would make sense for exact to automatically add a new line to the query string (if it is not already there)

I don't think this kind of ad-hoc change is good idea. I'd rather add `description_first_line()` (or maybe `subject()`?) instead.
I like the idea of adding a `subject()"` function. However, I still believe that setting the description to `X` and not being able to find it by searching for `exact:X` is _very_ surprising. The fact that jj adds a `\n` under the hood should not leak into the user interface.

Also, what's the point of an `exact` modifier that will _never_ work? AFACT currently exact never returns any revisions (except if you search for an empty string)! IMHO that means that `exact` is broken when used in combination with `describe()`.
> I still believe that setting the description to `X` and not being able to find it by searching for `exact:X` is _very_ surprising. The fact that jj adds a `\n` under the hood should not leak into the user interface.

I won't disagree that it's surprising, but the normalization rule isn't an implementation detail. It's something that an editor appends newline on save.

> Also, what's the point of an `exact` modifier that will _never_ work?

It works if you add `"\n"` (or the underlying commit description lacks `"\n"`.) It's weird if both `exact:"foo"` and `exact:"foo\n"` exactly matches the same data.

FWIW, `git`/`jj` CLI usually appends `"\n"`, but that's not guaranteed by Git data model.

Thank you @yuja, the new `subject()` PR you created is great.

Just FYI, while adding a \n is not a big deal on Linux or macOS, it is in fact quite hard on Windows unless you use the new PowerShell as your shell. Both cmd.exe and the old PS make it harder than you'd think. On cmd.exe you need to double the double quotes (e.g. `jj log -r "description(exact:""test\n"")"`), while on the old (default) PS we did not find a good solution.

Because of that, in addition to the inconsistency that I mentioned I still think that it would make sense for `describe(exact:X)` to add the `\n` for you if needed, but the proposed `subject()` function makes this less of a priority.
> it would make sense for `describe(exact:X)` to add the `\n` for you if needed

Since the trailing newline is not part of the data model, there can exist commits without a trailing newline. Since both the git and jj CLIs seem to consistently enforce the trailing newline, perhaps such commits would only be created by tools using the git or jj libraries (libgit2, jgit, gitoxide, jj-lib, etc.). So if `describe(exact:X)` adds the newline, then it would make it impossible to search for commits without a trailing newline.

I understand that the current behavior is confusing, but hopefully `describe(exact:X)` is kind of rare in practice and would usually show up only in scripts?
It's also weird that only the `exact:` pattern is handled differently. Suppose many use cases of `describe(exact:"non-empty-string")` can be served by `subject()`, I wouldn't want to introduce weird special case. If it's super confusing, I would rather add a warning.

def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import re
    from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET

    def strip_ansi(s: str) -> str:
        # CSI + a few common single-char escapes
        s = re.sub(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]", "", s)
        s = s.replace("\x1b", "")
        return s

    def merge_status(old: str | None, new: str) -> str:
        # prefer worst outcome
        order = {"pass": 0, "skip": 1, "fail": 2}
        if old is None:
            return new
        return new if order[new] > order[old] else old

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    text = strip_ansi(log).replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")

    # ---- JUnit-ish XML (best-effort, if embedded in logs) ----
    for m in re.finditer(r"(<testsuite\b.*?</testsuite>)", text, flags=re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE):
        chunk = m.group(1)
        try:
            root = ET.fromstring(chunk)
        except Exception:
            continue
        for tc in root.iter():
            tag = tc.tag.lower().split("}")[-1]
            if tag != "testcase":
                continue
            name = (tc.get("name") or "").strip()
            classname = (tc.get("classname") or "").strip()
            full = f"{classname}.{name}".strip(".") if classname else name
            if not full:
                continue
            status = "pass"
            for child in list(tc):
                ctag = child.tag.lower().split("}")[-1]
                if ctag in ("failure", "error"):
                    status = "fail"
                    break
                if ctag == "skipped":
                    status = "skip"
            results[full] = merge_status(results.get(full), status)

    lines = text.splitlines()

    # ---- Rust libtest / cargo test (robust to line wrapping) ----
    rust_status_map = {"ok": "pass", "ignored": "skip", "FAILED": "fail", "fail": "fail", "error": "fail"}
    rust_line_prefix = re.compile(r"^\s*test\s+")
    rust_done_re = re.compile(r"(?:\s|\.)+(ok|ignored|FAILED|fail|error)\s*$")
    rust_full_re = re.compile(r"^\s*test\s+(.+?)\s*\.\.\.\s*(ok|ignored|FAILED|fail|error)\s*$")

    buf = ""
    buffering = False

    def flush_buf():
        nonlocal buf, buffering
        if not buf:
            buffering = False
            return
        s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", buf.strip())
        m = rust_full_re.match(s)
        if m:
            name, st = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2)
            results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), rust_status_map.get(st, "fail"))
        buf = ""
        buffering = False

    for raw in lines:
        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
        if rust_line_prefix.match(line):
            flush_buf()
            buffering = True
            buf = line.strip()
            if rust_done_re.search(buf):
                flush_buf()
            continue
        if buffering:
            if not line.strip():
                flush_buf()
                continue
            buf += " " + line.strip()
            if rust_done_re.search(buf):
                flush_buf()
    flush_buf()

    # Rust failures sections / blocks
    in_failures = False
    for raw in lines:
        s = raw.rstrip()
        if s.strip() == "failures:":
            in_failures = True
            continue
        if in_failures and not s.strip():
            in_failures = False
            continue
        if in_failures:
            m = re.match(r"^\s*(\S+)\s*$", s)
            if m:
                results[m.group(1)] = merge_status(results.get(m.group(1)), "fail")

        m2 = re.match(r"^----\s+(.+?)\s+stdout\s+----\s*$", s)
        if m2:
            name = m2.group(1).strip()
            results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), "fail")

    # ---- pytest ----
    pytest_re = re.compile(r"^(?P<name>\S+::\S+)\s+(?P<status>PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS)\b")
    for raw in lines:
        m = pytest_re.match(raw.strip())
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group("name")
        st = m.group("status")
        status = "pass" if st == "PASSED" else "skip" if st in ("SKIPPED", "XFAIL") else "fail"
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    # ---- unittest/nose ----
    unittest_re = re.compile(r"^(?P<name>\S+)\s+\.\.\.\s+(?P<status>ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped)\s*$")
    for raw in lines:
        m = unittest_re.match(raw.strip())
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group("name")
        st = m.group("status")
        status = "pass" if st == "ok" else "skip" if st == "skipped" else "fail"
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    # ---- Go test ----
    go_re = re.compile(r"^---\s+(?P<status>PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(?P<name>\S+)")
    for raw in lines:
        m = go_re.match(raw.strip())
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group("name")
        st = m.group("status")
        status = "pass" if st == "PASS" else "skip" if st == "SKIP" else "fail"
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    # ---- Jest (basic) ----
    jest_re = re.compile(r"^(PASS|FAIL)\s+.+?\s+-\s+(?P<name>.+?)\s*$")
    for raw in lines:
        m = jest_re.match(raw.strip())
        if m:
            status = "pass" if m.group(1) == "PASS" else "fail"
            name = m.group("name")
            results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    jest_sym_re = re.compile(r"^\s*([✓✕○])\s+(?P<name>.+?)\s*$")
    for raw in lines:
        m = jest_sym_re.match(raw)
        if not m:
            continue
        sym = m.group(1)
        status = "pass" if sym == "✓" else "skip" if sym == "○" else "fail"
        name = m.group("name").strip()
        results[name] = merge_status(results.get(name), status)

    return results

problem_statement:
Apartment threaded IDispatch server throws `InvalidOperationException` or fails to marshal ### Description When implementing an IDispatch apartment threaded object on net7.0, an exception is thrown when calling `Marshal.GetIDispatchForObject`. Non-.Net callers get `E_NOINTERFACE`. The same code works on .Net Framework. This seems to be related to removing `[ComVisible(true)]` from many types - which is understandable in general, but `StandardOleMarshalObject` is exclusively used with COM. I would propose that `[ComVisible(true)]` be re-added to `StandardOleMarshalObject`, the requirement for `[ComVisible(true)]` to be reduced, or the need to re-implement `StandardOleMarshalObject` be documented. In testing, adding the attribute is sufficient to avoid the exception. ### Reproduction Steps Create a new `net7.0-windows` console program. Add the following to Program.cs: ```c# Marshal.GetIDispatchForObject(new Example()); [ComVisible(true)] public class Example : StandardOleMarshalObject { } ``` ### Expected behavior The example program should not throw an exception (the type will be available to IDispatch callers). ### Actual behavior The following exception is thrown: > System.InvalidOperationException: Type 'DispTarget' has a ComVisible(false) parent 'System.Runtime.InteropServices.StandardOleMarshalObject' in its hierarchy, therefore QueryInterface calls for IDispatch or class interfaces are disallowed.
    at System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal.GetIDispatchForObjectNative(Object o)
    at Program.<Main>$(String[] args) in C:\dev\source\repos\ComDispatchDemo\DemoDispatchServer\Program.cs:line 8 If the type is passed to a COM server or registered with `CoRegisterClassObject` instead of `GetIDispatchForObject`, no exception is thrown in the server and `E_NOINTERFACE` is returned the caller. ### Regression? Yes. The same code on net48 runs without issue. ### Known Workarounds Copy/paste the implementation of [StandardOleMarshalComObject.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d561f390b8085ffed309c49cf30ec205a47868c0/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/StandardOleMarshalObject.Windows.cs#L8) into the project, and add the `[ComVisible(true)]` attribute. Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/interop-contrib See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description When implementing an IDispatch apartment threaded object on net7.0, an exception is thrown when calling `Marshal.GetIDispatchForObject`. Non-.Net callers get `E_NOINTERFACE`. The same code works on .Net Framework. This seems to be related to removing `[ComVisible(true)]` from many types - which is understandable in general, but `StandardOleMarshalObject` is exclusively used with COM. I would propose that `[ComVisible(true)]` be re-added to `StandardOleMarshalObject`, the requirement for `[ComVisible(true)]` to be reduced, or the need to re-implement `StandardOleMarshalObject` be documented. In testing, adding the attribute is sufficient to avoid the exception. ### Reproduction Steps Create a new `net7.0-windows` console program. Add the following to Program.cs: ```c# Marshal.GetIDispatchForObject(new Example()); [ComVisible(true)] public class Example : StandardOleMarshalObject { } ``` ### Expected behavior The example program should not throw an exception (the type will be available to IDispatch callers). ### Actual behavior The following exception is thrown: > System.InvalidOperationException: Type 'DispTarget' has a ComVisible(false) parent 'System.Runtime.InteropServices.StandardOleMarshalObject' in its hierarchy, therefore QueryInterface calls for IDispatch or class interfaces are disallowed.
    at System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal.GetIDispatchForObjectNative(Object o)
    at Program.<Main>$(String[] args) in C:\dev\source\repos\ComDispatchDemo\DemoDispatchServer\Program.cs:line 8 If the type is passed to a COM server or registered with `CoRegisterClassObject` instead of `GetIDispatchForObject`, no exception is thrown in the server and `E_NOINTERFACE` is returned the caller. ### Regression? Yes. The same code on net48 runs without issue. ### Known Workarounds Copy/paste the implementation of [StandardOleMarshalComObject.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/d561f390b8085ffed309c49cf30ec205a47868c0/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Runtime/InteropServices/StandardOleMarshalObject.Windows.cs#L8) into the project, and add the `[ComVisible(true)]` attribute. Alternately, if the object does not require apartment threading, remove `StandardOleMarshalComObject` as a base class. ### Configuration dotnet 7.0.401 Windows 11 22H2 (22621.2428) Reproducible with `Platform` x86 or x64 Presumed to be applicable to .Net 5..8 and all platforms ### Other information Loosely related: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/80422

problem_statement: AZ executable doesn't launch properly on Windows After the release of version 0.3.2, we've found that the Azure CLI extension can no longer launch `az` properly. It always fails with an error like the one below: `An error occurred trying to start process 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft SDKs\Azure\CLI2\wbin\az' with working directory 'x'. The specified executable is not a valid application for this OS platform. ` ```System.ComponentModel.Win32Exception: at System.Diagnostics.Process.StartWithCreateProcess (System.Diagnostics.Process, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a) at AzureMcp.Services.ProcessExecution.ExternalProcessService+d__1.MoveNext (azmcp, Version=0.3.2.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null: D:\a\_work\1\s\src\Services\ProcessExecution\ExternalProcessService.cs:68) at System.Runtime.ExceptionServices.ExceptionDispatchInfo.Throw (System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e) at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter.ThrowForNonSuccess (System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e) at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter.HandleNonSuccessAndDebuggerNotification (System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e) at System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TaskAwaiter`1.GetResult (System.Private.CoreLib, Version=9.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=7cec85d7bea7798e) at AzureMcp.Areas.Extension.Commands.AzCommand+d__18.MoveNext (azmcp, Version=0.3.2.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=null: D:\a\_work\1\s\src\Areas\Extension\Commands\AzCommand.cs:169) ``` We've confirmed that version 0.3.1 works properly: We've replicated this behavior on Windows Server 2025 and Windows 11, where the AZ CLI was installed with MSI packages. On our systems, it seems we have an `az` bash script in the PATH: ``` PS C:\> where.exe az C:\Program Files\Microsoft SDKs\Azure\CLI2\wbin\az C:\Program Files\Microsoft SDKs\Azure\CLI2\wbin\az.cmd ``` We haven't been able to confirm, but it seems likely the new issue is related to https://github.com/Azure/azure-mcp/issues/351 and https://github.com/Azure/azure-mcp/pull/552. Thanks in advance!

def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """
    Robust TRX (Visual Studio TestRun) parser.

    Key issues handled:
    - Test output may contain hard line-wraps *inside* XML attribute values (e.g., testName="Azu\nre..."),
      which breaks names if parsed as XML (XML normalizes newlines to spaces inside attributes).
      We first "de-wrap" newlines that occur inside quoted attribute values.
    - Names and messages may contain XML/HTML entities (" etc.) -> unescaped.
    - Namespace/no-namespace TRX.
    - Fallback regex extraction if XML parse fails for any reason.
    """
    import re
    import html
    from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET

    def dewrap_newlines_inside_quotes(s: str) -> str:
        # Remove CR/LF that occur while we're inside a quoted attribute value.
        out = []
        in_quote = False
        quote_char = ""
        i = 0
        while i < len(s):
            ch = s[i]
            if not in_quote:
                if ch in ("'", '"'):
                    in_quote = True
                    quote_char = ch
                out.append(ch)
                i += 1
                continue

            # in_quote
            if ch == quote_char:
                in_quote = False
                quote_char = ""
                out.append(ch)
                i += 1
                continue

            # drop hard wraps inside quotes
            if ch == "\r":
                if i + 1 < len(s) and s[i + 1] == "\n":
                    i += 2
                else:
                    i += 1
                continue
            if ch == "\n":
                i += 1
                continue

            out.append(ch)
            i += 1
        return "".join(out)

    def normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
        # Decode entities; keep spaces as-is (but collapse accidental multi-spaces).
        name = html.unescape(name or "")
        name = re.sub(r"\s{2,}", " ", name).strip()
        return name

    def map_outcome(outcome: str) -> str:
        o = (outcome or "").strip().lower()
        if o == "passed":
            return "pass"
        if o in ("skipped", "notexecuted", "not executed"):
            return "skip"
        # failed/error/timeout/etc.
        return "fail"

    def worse_status(a: str, b: str) -> str:
        # fail > skip > pass
        rank = {"pass": 0, "skip": 1, "fail": 2}
        return a if rank.get(a, 0) >= rank.get(b, 0) else b

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    cleaned = log.lstrip("\ufeff")
    cleaned = dewrap_newlines_inside_quotes(cleaned)

    # 1) Prefer XML parsing (most accurate)
    try:
        root = ET.fromstring(cleaned)

        # Iterate all elements, ignore namespace.
        for elem in root.iter():
            tag = elem.tag.split("}", 1)[-1]  # drop namespace if any
            if tag != "UnitTestResult":
                continue

            name = normalize_name(elem.attrib.get("testName", ""))
            if not name:
                continue

problem_statement:
Add CreateNewProcessGroup to ProcessStartInfo
## Background and Motivation

<!--
We welcome API proposals! We have a process to evaluate the value and shape of new API. There is an overview of our process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/project/api-review-process.md). This template will help us gather the information we need to start the review process.
First, please describe the purpose and value of the new API here.
-->

_Edited by @jozkee_

Creating process groups is necessary to be able to send signals on Windows as they are sent to the whole group, you need to use `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` creation flag to isolate the signal from the parent process. POSIX systems have the same notion, however in unix-like systems one can use signals directly with processes.

This has been previously discussed in another issue in 2017 but it turned out that this change itself would not help the requesting team so it was dropped at that time. For the record, I am using proposals from that time.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/20734

## Proposed API
Expose the creation flag via a Windows-only property.
```diff
namespace System.Diagnostics
{
     public sealed partial class ProcessStartInfo
     {
+          [SupportedOSPlatform("windows")]
+          public bool CreateNewProcessGroup { get; set; }
     }
}
```

## Usage Examples

<!--
Please provide code examples that highlight how the proposed API additions are meant to be consumed.
This will help suggest whether the API has the right shape to be functional, performant and useable.
You can use code blocks like this:
-->
``` C#
var startInfo = new ProcessStartInfo
{
    FileName = "my-program.exe",
    CreateNewProcessGroup = true,
};
var p = new Process.Start(startInfo);
// Do some work...

GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(0 /* CTRL_C_EVENT */, (uint)process.Id)

[DllImport("kernel32.dll")]
[return: MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.Bool)]
public static extern bool GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(uint dwCtrlEvent, uint dwProcessGroupId);
```
## Alternative Designs

1. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/71515 was considered but I've opted for this proposal instead as we do have concrete scenarios for it.  

2. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/109432, diffrent property naming: `EnableConsoleControlEvents`.  This name makes sense if CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP has no other reason to be used for, outside of signal isolation, I'm unaware of more scenarios where this is useful but that can change in the future. 

## Risks
None

## Background and Motivation Creating process groups is necessary to be able to send signals on Windows as they are sent to the whole group and the calling process may not know the group ID itself. POSIX systems have the same notion, however in unix-like systems one can use signals directly with processes, which is impossible in Windows as I understand it. This has been previously discussed in another issue in 2017 but it turned out that this change itself would not help the requesting team so it was dropped at that time. For the record, I am using proposals from that time. https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/20734 ## Proposed API ```diff namespace System.Diagnostics { public sealed class ProcessStartInfo { + public bool CreateNewProcessGroup { get; set; } } } ``` ## Usage Examples ## Alternative Designs Alternative discussed in the linked issue was using creation flags such as: ``` C# [Flags] public enum CreationFlags { CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE = 0x00000010, **CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP = 0x00000200**, CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB = 0x010000000, CREATE_DEFAULT_ERROR_MODE = 0x04000000, ... }; ``` But this turns somewhat Windows-centric which is not desired. Using a bool property instead is similar to how `CreateNoWindow` is exposed in ProcessStartInfo. ## Risks I do not have deep knowledge on this subject but I do not see any risks. I would assume the default behavior would be kept the same so no breaking changes to existing code. I do not know of any circumstances where creating a process in new group would prevent the process from creation (such as clashing with CreateNoWindow flag), but that is potential risk. Stopping applications properly may be more challenging for developers using this as the spawned processes may not get signals generated by user interaction with terminal.
Author: mladedav
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Diagnostics.Process`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -
If I get this correctly, in order to obtain the same behaviour as `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Unix we would need to call `setpgid(0, 0);` between [fork and execve](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2544c744d204c6ae0e20ba78c9cb8832a92091f3/src/libraries/Native/Unix/System.Native/pal_process.c#L438)? I believe so. That would put the new process into a new process group with ID identical to that new process' ID. My concern about this proposal is that it seems to only allow a very constrained use case for process groups. What if I wanted to create a process group that includes the current process? It is probably telling that in the [original issue](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/20734#issuecomment-304395962) it was determined that ProcessStartInfo is probably not the appropriate API for making this type of configuration. So if we can't provide a general-purpose solution here, perhaps we shouldn't be adding it at all. As I understand the comment, ProcessStartInfo wasn't appropriate for the advanced usage PaulHigin needed, not for the flag itself. I can't think of a better place for this since this needs to be set before the process is started, but I do not mind it being anywhere else. The constraints are based on what both Windows and Linux can do - Windows only has a flag `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` for `CreaetProcess*` functions while Linux is able to change the group ID dynamically after fork. If you want the new process to be part of the creating process' group, you simply don't specify the option, it is the default in both OSs. Triage: We should do research and find out if Windows allows for modifying process group after process creation as Unix does. If it does, we should consider adding APIs for all possibilities: - getting and setting process group of a given process instance - specify it during creating If it's not possible, the current proposal looks as good as it is. Note: as @mladedav initially pointed out, the primary goal of this feature is to allow sending signals to the process on Windows. If `Process` somehow exposed this functionality directly (e.g. with a `process.SendSignal(...)` method), then this switch would not be needed and may become an implementation detail (i.e. `Process.Start(...)` may still create a new process group, just not expose it to the caller). I am affected by this as well in a very similar way to the above mentioned issue (https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-dotnet/issues/124) Wanted to comment on this just to show there is a want for this, as the previous issue was closed due to lack of use by devs. Any updates? > We should do research and find out if Windows allows for modifying process group after process creation as Unix does. If it does, we should consider adding APIs for all possibilities: > * getting and setting process group of a given process instance > * specify it during creating Please note the restriction on modifying the process group of an existing other process using `setpgid`: this can only be done if the target process has not called `execve` or a similar function yet. In fact, that form of the call is only intended to allow the parent process to ensure the process group has been set in the absence of other synchronization (such as the pipe .NET uses to obtain the return value from `execve`). The child process should always set its own process group ID (if the parent's process group ID is unsuitable). If the parent process encounters the error condition `[EACCES]` that the target process has already called `execve`, the process group has already been set, so the parent process needs to ignore the error. Instead, the extra possibilities of `setpgid` are for two use cases: * Create multiple child processes and have all of them join a single new process group. Most job control shells such as bash and zsh do this for pipelines. This allows all elements of a pipeline access to the terminal while also allowing the shell to wait for and check the exit status of all elements, and not creating any additional processes. * In a job control shell, set the shell's process group ID to the shell's process ID, and attempt to undo that when disabling job control mode (such as when suspending the shell itself). If someone wants to do this from .NET, I'd say platform invoke is fine. Documentation should warn that starting a process in a new process group may have unexpected effects if the process has a controlling terminal. In particular, the child process will not receive signals from key combinations such as Ctrl+C and will be suspended if it tries to read from the terminal (the kernel assuming that the parent process will deal with that). If the process does not have a controlling terminal, creating new process groups is fine and allows sending signals to whole trees of processes except those that actively change their process group ID. If Windows provides no way to create multiple child processes and have all of them join a single new process group, the `CreateNewProcessGroup` boolean is certainly sufficient. @jilles-sg I updated the API proposal yesterday to reflect this will be a Windows-only API to unblock sending signals to an isolated process group. There won't be any effects in Unix.

Global tracer from start-up extension

     but: was "io.opentelemetry.api.trace.DefaultTracer"

cd microprofile/telemetry

test_cmds: & "C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\lib\maven\apache-maven-3.9.12\bin\mvn.cmd" -Ptests test -DtrimStackTrace=false "-Dsurefire.printSummary=true" -DfailIfNoTests=false
log_parser:
def parser(log: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    import re

    results: dict[str, str] = {}

    def add_result(test_id: str, status: str):
        if not test_id:
            return
        test_id = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", test_id).strip()
        if test_id:
            results[test_id] = status

    # --------- 1) JUnit/Surefire XML parsing (robust to wrapped output) ---------
    chunks = re.split(r"^===FILE===.*$", log, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    for chunk in chunks:
        if "<testcase" not in chunk:
            continue

        # Scan each testsuite region (can be multiple per chunk)
        for m in re.finditer(r"<testsuite\b", chunk, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
            sub = chunk[m.start():]
            end = re.search(r"</testsuite\s*>", sub, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
            xml = sub[: end.end()] if end else sub

            # Repair console hard-wraps by flattening newlines inside XML
            xml_flat = re.sub(r"\r?\n", "", xml)

            tc_re = re.compile(
                r"<testcase\b(?P<attrs>[^>/]*?)(?:\s*/\s*>|>(?P<body>.*?)</testcase\s*>)",
                flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL,
            )
            attr_re = re.compile(r'(\w+)\s*=\s*"([^"]*)"', flags=re.DOTALL)

            for tm in tc_re.finditer(xml_flat):
                attrs = dict(attr_re.findall(tm.group("attrs") or ""))
                name = (attrs.get("name") or "").strip()
                classname = (attrs.get("classname") or "").strip()
                if not name:
                    continue

                test_id = f"{classname}#{name}" if classname else name
                body = tm.group("body") or ""

                status = "pass"
                if re.search(r"<skipped\b", body, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
                    status = "skip"
                if re.search(r"<failure\b|<error\b", body, flags=re.IGNORECASE):
                    status = "fail"

                add_result(test_id, status)

    # --------- 2) Fallback parsers for other frameworks ---------
    # pytest: file.py::test_name PASSED/FAILED/SKIPPED/ERROR
    for m in re.finditer(
        r"^(?P<name>\S+::\S+)\s+(?P<status>PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED|ERROR)\b",
        log,
        flags=re.MULTILINE,
    ):
        st = m.group("status")
        status = "pass" if st == "PASSED" else ("skip" if st == "SKIPPED" else "fail")
        add_result(m.group("name"), status)

    # unittest: package.Class.test_method ... ok/FAIL/ERROR/skipped
    for m in re.finditer(
        r"^(?P<name>[A-Za-z_]\w*(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*)+)\s+\.\.\.\s+(?P<status>ok|FAIL|ERROR|skipped)\b",
        log,
        flags=re.MULTILINE,
    ):
        st = m.group("status").lower()
        status = "pass" if st == "ok" else ("skip" if st == "skipped" else "fail")
        add_result(m.group("name"), status)

    # go test: --- PASS/FAIL/SKIP: TestName
    for m in re.finditer(
        r"^---\s+(?P<status>PASS|FAIL|SKIP):\s+(?P<name>\S+)",
        log,
        flags=re.MULTILINE,
    ):
        st = m.group("status")
        status = "pass" if st == "PASS" else ("skip" if st == "SKIP" else "fail")
        add_result(m.group("name"), status)

    # jest-ish: PASS/FAIL <name>
    for m in re.finditer(
        r"^(?P<status>PASS|FAIL)\s+(?P<name>.+?)\s*$",
        log,
        flags=re.MULTILINE,
    ):
        status = "pass" if m.group("status") == "PASS" else "fail"
        add_result(m.group("name"), status)

    return results
